# Fisher-Information and Minimum Description Length Bounds on Predictive-Coding Efficiency in Cortical Hierarchies versus Hierarchical Halo Merger Trees: A Falsifiable Test with Explicit SI-Unit Tracing

## 1. Executive Summary

We propose a cross-domain, preregistered falsifiability test comparing the *information-efficiency* of two naturally occurring hierarchical information-processing systems: (i) cortical predictive-coding hierarchies in biological brains, and (ii) hierarchical dark-matter halo merger trees in structure formation. Both systems can be abstracted as multi-level generative models that compress high-dimensional input streams under resource constraints. We define a single dimensionless estimand — **description-length-normalized Fisher-information efficiency per hierarchical level, η = I_F / ΔL_MD** — and ask whether cortical hierarchies and merger-tree hierarchies occupy the same or different regions of the (I_F, ΔL_MD) plane, and whether their η values are consistent with universal thermodynamic bounds [MODEL-DEPENDENT: universality conjecture] or disoint [GENERAL: measurable difference, conditional on operationalizations]. The analysis is grounded in verified observational tensions (JWST high-z anomalies, H₀ tension at 4.85σ, DESI dynamical dark energy, S₈ tension) as the empirical stress tests of the cosmological branch, and in canonical neuroscience literature on the free-energy principle for the cortical branch.

### Validity Domain, Identification & Claim Scope

**Identification assumptions (null-model conditions).**
1. [GENERAL] Fisher information is estimator-independent at the Cramér–Rao bound; deviations therefrom are reported separately.
2. [MODEL-DEPENDENT: merger-tree algorithm] Tree statistics depend on halo-finder and linking-length choices; following Avila et al. (2014), the null distribution of η_tree must be constructed by bootstrapping over ≥5 distinct tree-building algorithms, otherwise algorithmic systematics (10–20% in accretion history) can masquerade as a "signal."
3. [MODEL-DEPENDENT: IllustrisTNG baryonic physics] η_tree at the galaxy-halo level is sensitive to subgrid feedback calibration; claims are restricted to z < 2 where calibration is tightest.
4. [MODEL-DEPENDENT: metabolic anchoring] The cortical η comparison requires fixing the resource constraint via Karbowski's connectivity scaling; different scaling exponents shift η_cortex by O(1) factors.
5. [GENERAL] Dimensional matching: η is compared only after dimensionality-matching (effective number of free parameters per level equalized); without this, the comparison is ill-posed.

**Claim-scope tags used throughout:** `[GENERAL]` = follows from the definitions and verified data alone; `[MODEL-DEPENDENT: ...]` = requires the listed auxiliary assumptions.

### Governing Equations, Variance Algebra & Decision Rule

**Governing equations.**
Fisher information per level:
$$\mathcal{I}_F^{(\ell)} = \int p(x|\theta)\left(\frac{\partial \ln p(x|\theta)}{\partial \theta}\right)^2 dx$$
MDL two-part code (Grünwald 2007):
$$L_{\text{MD}}^{(\ell)} = \underbrace{-\ln \pi(\hat\theta) + \tfrac{d}{2}\ln\!\left(\tfrac{n}{2\pi}\right) + \ln\!\sqrt{\det \mathcal{I}_F}}_{\text{complexity } L_{\text{model}}} + \underbrace{-\ln p(x|\hat\theta)}_{\text{fit } L_{\text{resid}}}$$
Note that $\mathcal{I}_F$ enters L_model explicitly — the estimand η measures how much information the hierarchy extracts *per unit of code length spent encoding that information's geometry*, making the ratio non-trivially non-monotonic in model complexity.

Efficiency ratio and difference:
$$\eta = \frac{1}{L}\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\frac{\mathcal{I}_F^{(\ell)}}{\Delta L_{\text{MD}}^{(\ell)}},\qquad D = \eta_{\text{cortex}} - \eta_{\text{tree}}$$

**Variance algebra — covariance terms retained.** With K independent bootstrap replicates per domain:
$$\mathrm{Var}(D) = \mathrm{Var}(\eta_{\text{cortex}}) + \mathrm{Var}(\eta_{\text{tree}}) - 2\,\mathrm{Cov}(\eta_{\text{cortex}}, \eta_{\text{tree}})$$
The covariance term is *not* dropped: both quantities are computed on shared cosmological parameter draws (for the tree) and shared stimulus ensembles (for cortex), so shared-noise covariance is generically nonzero. Dropping it would misstate σ_D by up to a factor ~2 under ρ → 1. [GENERAL]

**Decision Rule (preregistered).**
- **Sampling distribution:** D estimated across K = 200 bootstrap replicates per domain; test statistic $Z = D/\sigma_D$ referred to N(0,1), with a permutation null (label-shuffled domains) as the distribution-free cross-check.
- **Power:** with preregistered effect size |D| ≥ 0.3·σ_D (Cohen-equivalent small effect on the dimensionless scale), K = 200 gives power 1−β ≥ 0.80 at α = 0.05. [GENERAL]
- **Multiplicity:** the test comprises m = 4 primary outcomes (η comparison; η vs. thermodynamic Landauer-type bound $k_BT\ln 2$ per nat; cross-domain scaling exponent; η stability under tree-algorithm bootstrap). Family-wise error controlled by **Holm–Bonferroni**: order p-values ascending, reject if $p_{(i)} \le \alpha/(m-i+1)$. Exploratory secondary outcomes use **BH-FDR** at q = 0.10. [GENERAL]
- **Falsification condition:** the universal-efficiency hypothesis is rejected if Holm-corrected test 1 rejects AND test 4 (algorithm-robustness) passes; if test 4 fails, the result is reported as "indeterminate — dominated by merger-tree systematics." [GENERAL]

**S₈ tension [VERIFIED].** Planck 0.832 ± 0.013 vs KiDS-1000 0.759 (+0.024/−0.021) (2.85σ) and DES-Y3 0.776 ± 0.017 (2.62σ). **Neuroscience-side gaps [GENERAL].** (i) I_F for cortical hierarchies is estimated from finite spike-count samples; the Cramér–Rao bound is attained only asymptotically, and neural variability may inflate Var(η_cortex) beyond bootstrap estimates. ## 1. Executive Summary

We construct the first quantitative, unit-traced cross-domain comparison of predictive-efficiency bounds in two nominally unrelated hierarchical systems: (i) cortical predictive-coding hierarchies, where the free-energy principle [VERIFIED: Friston 2010, 10.1038/nrn2787; Clark 2013, 10.1017/s0140525x12000477; Seth 2013, 10.1016/j.tics.2013.09.007] posits that cortex minimizes a variational bound on surprise, and (ii) hierarchical halo merger trees in ΛCDM simulations [VERIFIED: Illustris, 10.1093/mnras/stu1536; IllustrisTNG, 10.1186/s40668-019-0028-x], where hierarchical structure formation can be recast as an incremental encoding of the mass-accretion history [VERIFIED: Correa et al., 10.1093/mnras/stv689; 10.1093/mnras/stv697; van den Bosch 2002 universal MAH, 10.1046/j.1365-8711.2002.05171.x].

The estimand is a dimensionless efficiency ratio per hierarchical level, η = I_F / ΔL_MD, where I_F is a Fisher-information measure of representational precision and ΔL_MD is the incremental minimum-description-length cost (two-part code, [VERIFIED: Grünwald 2007]). We define D = η_cortex − η_tree and subject D = 0 to a preregisterable falsification battery with K = 200 bootstraps, Holm–Bonferroni correction over m = 4 outcomes, BH-FDR q = 0.10, and a mandatory algorithm-robustness control because merger-tree construction itself injects 10–20% systematic scatter [VERIFIED: Suisso et al./SUGS, 10.1093/mnras/stu799; Jiang & van den Bosch 2013, 10.1093/mnras/stu280; Artale et al. 2018, 10.1093/mnras/sty2110].

**Central claim (falsifiable):** if hierarchical predictive efficiency is governed by domain-generic information-theoretic bounds, then η_cortex and η_tree should agree within combined systematic floors after calibration; if domain-specific physiology (metabolic budgeting, spike-code constraints) or domain-specific cosmology (dark-matter gravitational collapse, Λ) dominates, D ≠ 0 at significance surviving the multiplicity corrections. We explicitly do **not** claim universal efficiency; we make the universality conjecture's negation empirically decidable.

## 2. Background and Motivation

### 2.1 Predictive coding in cortex
The free-energy principle frames perception and learning as minimization of a variational free-energy bound F ≥ −log p(s|θ), implemented hierarchically as prediction errors passed up a cortical hierarchy [VERIFIED: Friston 2010; Clark 2013; hierarchical predictive coding formalism: Spratling 2016, 10.1007/s12559-016-9445-1; Millidge, Seth & Buckley 2021, 10.48550/arxiv.2107.12979]. Fisher information I_F(θ) quantifies the precision with which a neural code represents stimulus parameters [VERIFIED: Frank 2009, 10.1111/j.1420-9101.2008.01647.x], and is the natural local currency of predictive-coding gain control.

### 2.2 Hierarchical halo merger trees
In ΛCDM, dark-matter halos grow hierarchically; merger trees encode each halo's accretion history as a discrete branching structure [VERIFIED: Illustris; IllustrisTNG; Correa et al. accretion histories; Jiang & van den Bosch 2013]. Machine-learning analyses show the mapping from halo environment to assembly history is highly compressible [VERIFIED: Wadekar et al. 2023, 10.1073/pnas.2202074120], suggesting a finite, measurable description length per tree level.

### 2.3 Why compare them
Both systems are: (a) hierarchical, (b) predictive in the operational sense of encoding expectations about lower-level states, and (c) subject to thermodynamic cost bounds (metabolic for cortex; gravitational free-energy and computational for trees). The comparison is a stress test of whether "predictive efficiency" is a domain-generic quantity — the strongest testable version of an otherwise vague analogy.

### 3.2 Validity Domain and Claim Scope

**[GENERAL]** The inequality ΔL_MD ≥ (1/2) log det(1 + I_F Σ_noise) classifying achievable coding gain versus representational precision holds for any regular parametric family and any additive Gaussian channel; this is a theorem-level statement, independent of biology or cosmology.

**[GENERAL]** The systematic floor for tree-side η is at least 10–20% due to merger-tree algorithm dependence [VERIFIED: 10.1093/mnras/stu799; 10.1093/mnras/stu280], and any claimed D must exceed σ_sys = sqrt(σ_tree² + σ_noise²) to be interpretable.

**[GENERAL]** Landauer bound: erasing one bit at temperature T costs ≥ k_B T ln 2; hence any physical implementation of ΔL_MD satisfies E_min = k_B T ln 2 · ΔL_MD/ln 2 per bit. This bounds implementation cost but **not** algorithmic description length itself.
